title: Skin-Deep: A Geometric Diagnostic for Alignment Fragility in Large Language Model Representations
abstract: arXiv:2606.22676v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Refusal on a safety benchmark does not reveal how stable that behavior will remain after model updates. Benign downstream fine-tuning can weaken refusal, yet behavioral evaluations typically expose this fragility only after an intervention. We introduce SKIN-DEEP, a geometric diagnostic that examines the unmodified model's residual-stream activations. It compares aligned and base checkpoints to identify safety-separating directions, tests their behavioral relevance through ablation, and summarizes the layer-wise pattern in the Geometric Fragility Score (GFS). Across twenty-one instruction-tuned models, harmful requests and benign instructions exhibit a recurring low-rank separation pattern. Selected direction ablations weaken refusal, with the effective direction varying across models. translated_title: 浮于表层：大语言模型表示中对齐脆弱性的几何诊断方法
translated_abstract: 在安全基准测试上的拒绝行为并不能揭示该行为在模型更新之后能保持多稳定。良性的下游微调可能会削弱模型的拒绝能力，然而行为评估通常只有在实施干预之后才能暴露这种脆弱性。我们提出了SKIN-DEEP，一种几何诊断方法，它检查未经修改的模型的残差流激活。该方法通过比较对齐模型与基础模型检查点来识别安全分离方向，通过消融实验测试这些方向的行为相关性，并将逐层模式总结为几何脆弱性得分。在二十一个指令微调模型上，有害请求与良性指令呈现出反复出现的低秩分离模式。对选定方向进行消融会削弱模型的拒绝行为，且有效方向因模型而异。在良性低秩微调实验中，微调前得分最低的最初安全模型具有最低的有害服从率。
tldr: 提出了SKIN-DEEP几何诊断方法，通过分析模型残差流激活中安全分离方向的逐层模式计算几何脆弱性得分（GFS），无需干预即可预测模型在良性微调后拒绝有害请求能力的稳定性。
